tagline: 7,641 islands, one archipelagic nation — the country that has to move on water.
summary: The Philippines is the clearest national case for marine mobility on Earth: a 7,641-island archipelago of 115 million people where inter-island travel is not a luxury but the basic condition of the economy. Today that movement runs on slow RoRo ferries and weather-exposed bangka pumpboats. A clean, fast foiling tier is the missing layer between the airport and the island.
why_marine_mobility: No single city brief can tell the Philippine story, because the story IS the water between the islands. Manila to Palawan, Cebu across to Bohol, the Caticlan gateway to Boracay, the Camotes and Romblon chains — these are not edge cases, they are how the nation commutes, trades, and holidays. The current options are a 90-minute flight that skips the journey, or a multi-hour ferry that endures it. Navier's Pioneer II foiling tier turns a rough 2-hour crossing into a smooth 40-minute glide, and the Quanta-LR hybrid range opens trunk corridors that no day-boat can reach.

use_cases.body: Caticlan to Boracay: replace the crowded pumpboat transfer with a smooth, dry, premium foiling shuttle into the country's flagship beach destination.
Cebu to Bohol: a 30-nautical-mile corridor between two of the Visayas' largest economies, run today on conventional fast-craft — ideal for a clean Pioneer II tier.
Manila to Palawan: a long-range Quanta-LR trunk linking the capital to El Nido, Coron and Amanpulo — a journey that is itself the destination.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The Visayas inter-island corridors (Cebu–Bohol, Cebu–Camotes, Caticlan–Boracay, the Romblon chain) sit comfortably inside Pioneer II's 70-nautical-mile range at 30 knots — commercial-ready today.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The Manila–Palawan trunk and other long-haul inter-island links are Quanta-LR territory (~700 nm hybrid range, H2 2026+), unlocking corridors no battery day-boat can serve.

signature_routes.label: Manila → Palawan (El Nido / Coron / Amanpulo) — national long-range hero
Cebu ↔ Bohol (Tagbilaran) — the Visayas economic corridor
Caticlan ↔ Boracay — the flagship resort gateway

transit_planning: For a national authority or a super-app operator: a premium, low-emission water tier that relieves congested airports on short island hops, restores weather-resilient service on corridors that ferries cancel, and gives the inter-island journey the dignity of the destination. Start with the proven Visayas corridors on Pioneer II, then extend trunk routes on Quanta-LR as range comes online.
competitive_landscape: Inter-island travel today splits between domestic aviation (fast but skips the journey and clogs regional airports) and conventional ferries / bangka pumpboats (affordable but slow, rough and weather-vulnerable). Navier's foiling tier is the missing premium-but-practical middle: faster than any ferry, smoother than any pumpboat, cleaner than both, and reachable in-app.
regulatory_note: Domestic sea transport is regulated by MARINA (the Maritime Industry Authority) and the Philippine Coast Guard; inter-island commercial operation requires MARINA franchise and vessel certification. Engagement with MARINA's regional offices (e.g. Region VII / Cebu) is the natural first regulatory step.
seasonality: The dry season (Nov–May) offers the calmest crossings; the southwest monsoon (Habagat, Jun–Oct) and typhoon season bring rougher seas and ferry cancellations — precisely the conditions where a stabilised foiling craft holds its schedule best.

precedents.what: Four Seasons Lake Austin operates an N30 in live luxury-hospitality service — proof of the premium water-shuttle model Navier is bringing to archipelagic markets.
